title: unit-gap-artefacts: machine-checkable artefacts for a refutation of Theorem 2 of arXiv:2603.08033
description:
DRAT proof certificates, exhaustive NPN-class gap censuses, exact-synthesis encoders, and a Lean 4 formalization supporting a refutation of Theorem 2 of Krinkin, The Unit Gap: How Sharing Works in Boolean Circuits (arXiv:2603.08033).

What this is not: progress on P vs NP. It is a correction to one published claim about the gap between DAG-optimal and formula-optimal And-Inverter Graph size, plus the data behind it.

The counterexample is parity on three inputs, where the DAG optimum is 6 gates and the formula optimum is 9, so the gap is 3 rather than the claimed maximum of 1.

The refutation itself is classical. The AIG basis with free inversions is exactly U2 — the full binary basis minus XOR and XNOR — so Schnorr (1976) gives opt = 6, an equality restated in the openly accessible Morizumi (arXiv:1504.06731) since the 1976 original is paywalled; and Khrapchenko's bound forces tree >= 9 leaves, hence >= 8 gates. That alone contradicts Theorem 2, with no computation of ours in the chain. The basis identification is elementary, but it is a step, and it is supplied by the accompanying note rather than by Schnorr or Khrapchenko.

The exact value 3 is a different matter: it needs tree = 9, which is not in the refereed literature. The obvious citation does not survive — Lee's rank technique (STACS 2007) was announced as determining the formula size of parity for every n, and Lee has since publicly retracted that claim. So tree = 9 is certified here, by two independent dynamic programs and the Lean development, and it agrees with the exhaustive enumeration of Cox and Healy (2011). At n = 4 the exact gap is classical again, via Schnorr and Tarui (2010), who showed Khrapchenko's bound is attained at powers of two.

An exhaustive census over the 222 NPN classes of n = 4 finds 72 classes (32.4%) with gap at least 2, the maximum being 6 — which is what Schnorr and Tarui give for parity-4. That is an external spot check on one row of the census, not on the other 221.

Re-checking that the archived CNFs are unsatisfiable needs drat-trim and nothing else. What a DRAT proof does not certify is that a CNF asks the right question; that is discharged separately, by an independent brute-force enumerator that shares no code with the SAT encoder. See README.md for the claim-to-file table and the re-check command.
